parsed.summary: The file defines the k-colour triangle Ramsey number R_k(3) as the least n such that every k-colouring of the edges of K_n (on Fin n) has a monochromatic triangle. It states four results: R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞; an explicit lower bound (c₀·k^{1/3}/log k)^k ≤ R_k(3) for k ≥ 2 together with the same limit; log R_k(3) lies between (1/3−ε)·k·log k and (1+ε)·k·log k eventually; and log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k). The main caveat is that the paper only asserts the existence of an absolute constant c, while the Lean statement fixes c₀ = 1/(6e^38), a value that is not in the excerpt. The upper-bound half of the log-sharp statements comes from the classical factorial bound, which the paper cites but does not prove in the excerpt.

glossary.plain: A k-edge-colouring C of K_n is triangle-free if, for every colour i, the graph of colour-i edges has no 3-clique.
glossary.standard_concept: No monochromatic triangle in an edge colouring of K_n.

glossary.plain: Every k-colouring of the edges of K_n on Fin n contains a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.standard_concept: n ≥ R_k(3) (the Ramsey property for n vertices).
glossary.note: For k = 0 and n ≥ 2 there are no labelings, so the property holds vacuously. This is irrelevant to the asymptotic statements.

glossary.plain: The least n such that every k-colouring of K_n has a monochromatic triangle, written R_k(3).
glossary.note: sInf ∅ = 0 would be junk. For k ≥ 1 the set is nonempty by Ramsey's theorem. Monotonicity in n is not needed, because the sInf is the least n directly.

lean_claims.plain: As k → ∞, R_k(3)^{1/k} tends to +∞ (as a real number).
For every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large k, (1/3−ε)·k·log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε)·k·log k.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) as k → ∞.

paper_claims.plain: There is an absolute constant c > 0 such that for all k ≥ 2, R_k(3) ≥ (c·k^{1/3}/log k)^k.
Combined with the factorial upper bound (2), k^{(1/3−o(1))k} ≤ R_k(3) ≤ k^{(1+o(1))k}, so R_k(3) = k^{Θ(k)}.

Taking logs, the o(1) terms become ε-bounds eventually in k. The upper bound relies on the cited factorial bound.
log R_k = Θ(k log k) is the standard reading of k^{Θ(k)}.
